title: Writing a hub setting refreshes the coordinator but not readings, so every control snaps back to its old value for up to a minute
rationale: H500HubControl.apply promises "one poll after the write ... so the new value is not guessed at", but the poll it triggers only fetches hub_status when self._polls is a multiple of _status_every, which is round(60/2)=30 at the default 2s interval. So roughly 29 out of 30 writes leave self.readings holding the pre-write value, and the LED / loop-recording / auto-upgrade / face-detection switches, the siren volume and duration numbers, and the siren-tone select all revert in the frontend and stay reverted until the next scheduled status fetch. The siren entity has the same problem on its own async_request_refresh calls. A one-shot "status is due next poll" flag fixes all of them at once without adding hub round trips.

title: The recordings card's day pager shows roughly two local days under the label of one
rationale: dayWindow returns the two UTC dates a local day touches, then api.recordings expands each date to a whole UTC day, producing a 48-hour UTC window. Neither the card nor the service clips the result back to the local day, so paging back one day lists the previous evening and most of today as well, under a label naming a single date. The rolling window gets away with the same widening because its far end is the future and holds no clips; a paged day has real recordings on both sides. Filtering the response to the local day in the card's _load when _dayOffset > 0 is the smallest fix.

title: Every preview thumbnail re-fetches the whole paired-camera list from the hub instead of using the cached one
rationale: The preview view already has the coordinator in hand, and the coordinator caches self.cameras precisely because the call is expensive; its own comment measures it at 58ms and refreshes it only every 300 seconds. But the view calls client.camera_at, which calls client.cameras() unconditionally, so opening a recordings card with N undownloaded clips issues N extra getGeneralDeviceList round trips on top of N media sessions, against hardware the whole codebase treats as easy to overload. Replacing camera_at with a bounds-checked coordinator.cameras[index] removes the round trip entirely.

title: The automatic-download path stats the media directory from inside the event loop
rationale: existing_clip performs two Path.exists() calls, and _download invokes it twice directly rather than through an executor, so every automatic download does blocking filesystem I/O on the event loop. The codebase states its own convention plainly in both other callers, which wrap the identical call — this is the one place that does not. Cheap to fix and it removes a latency source from the loop that also runs the poller.

title: Bad credentials retry the hub login forever: no ConfigEntryAuthFailed, no reauth flow
rationale: async_setup_entry turns every connect() failure into ConfigEntryNotReady, so a permanent auth failure (changed camera-account or cloud password) makes Home Assistant retry setup on a backoff indefinitely, buying a fresh hub login every retry — on hardware the repo's own test docstring says "is known to wedge under repeated logins and to recover only on a timeout". Raising ConfigEntryAuthFailed for the auth case stops the retry loop and opens the standard reauth prompt instead; it removes logins rather than adding any. The config flow has the same blind spot: a wrong password is reported as cannot_connect, so the owner is told the hub is unreachable when it is not. Needs async_step_reauth/async_step_reauth_confirm plus an invalid_auth string in both translation files.

title: The preview view accepts any start_time, opening an unbounded media session per request and 500ing with a traceback on out-of-range values

title: Every doorbell event publishes a 12-hour, credential-free signed media URL into its state attributes
rationale: The event entity writes a signed /media/local/... URL into the `image` attribute on every trigger. Because _own_frame runs in a coordinator callback with no request or websocket context, async_sign_path falls back to the content-user refresh token, so the resulting URL needs no Home Assistant login at all — anyone holding the string can fetch the frame for 12 hours. Entity attributes are readable by every authenticated user regardless of entity permissions, are persisted by the recorder for the purge window (default 10 days, well past the signature's own expiry), and ride along in automation traces. This is plainly a deliberate trade — mobile notification images cannot send an auth header, and the code comments say so — but 12 hours is far longer than that use case needs, and nothing documents that the attribute is a bearer credential. Worth weighing rather than assuming: shortening URL_LIFETIME would break 'open the notification the next morning', so the honest options are a shorter lifetime for the attribute specifically, or a note in the docs.

rationale: `set hass` stores the new state map but only renders on the very first call, so the only periodic render is the 60s poll. `live` is computed at render time against a 45s window, so a detection is only ever shown if a render happens to land inside those 45 seconds — roughly 3 renders in 4, and up to 45s late. title: The 60-second poll rebuilds innerHTML wholesale, restarting any open <video> from zero with autoplay
rationale: `_load()` always calls `_render()` in its finally, and `_render()` assigns `this._card.innerHTML`, destroying and recreating every child. `this._playing` survives a reload, so the player is re-emitted as a brand-new `<video controls autoplay>` — a user watching or paused mid-clip gets yanked back to 0:00 and force-played once a minute. The cheap root-cause fix is to keep the last rendered HTML string in a field and skip the assignment when it is unchanged (do not read `innerHTML` back — the browser reserializes it); that preserves the video element and the scroll position on every no-op poll, and pairs with candidate 3.

The event entity, the presses-only download` / `filter and all four cards read the same list...`; docs/reference.md:216-217 `Once a doorbell press has been identified and its code added to` / `\`RING_ALARM_TYPES\`, presses classify as \`ring\`...`; docs/protocol-notes.md:577-578 `**Which code means a doorbell press is still unknown.** \`RING_ALARM_TYPES\` in` / `\`const.py\` is deliberately empty; add the code there once a real press has been`. Contradicted by custom_components/tapo_h500/const.py:302 `RING_ALARM_TYPES: set[int] = {17}` and docs/limitations.md:99 `**Doorbell presses are identified.** \`alarm_type\` 17 is a press, confirmed`.

title: README and reference.md quote translation keys as entity IDs for four entities that actually get name-derived IDs
rationale: Entities set `_attr_has_entity_name = True`, so Home Assistant slugifies the *display name*, not the translation key, into the entity_id. Four documented IDs therefore do not exist. The worst is the README's no-internet setup step, which is load-bearing for the project's core mission and names a switch the user cannot find. reference.md already gets the sibling switches right (`switch.*_status_led`), so this is inconsistency, not a convention.
evidence: README.md:29 `- **Turn the auto-upgrade switch off** (\`switch.<hub>_auto_upgrade\`) — it` but translations/en.json has switch key `auto_upgrade` with `"name": "Automatic firmware updates"` → real id `switch.<hub>_automatic_firmware_updates` (which docs/reference.md:36 itself uses). README.md:117 `- **In one word:** \`sensor.<camera>_activity_level\` — quiet, active, busy or` and docs/reference.md:68 `| \`sensor.<name>_activity_level\` | The last hour in one word...` but sensor key `activity_level` has `"name": "Activity"` → real id `sensor.<camera>_activity`. docs/reference.md:25 `| \`sensor.*_auto_upgrade_time\` | The hour the hub installs firmware...` but sensor key `auto_upgrade_time` has `"name": "Automatic update time"` → real id `sensor.*_automatic_update_time`. custom_components/tapo_h500/entity.py:19 `_attr_has_entity_name = True`.

title: reference.md documents 7 of 8 cards, miscounts them twice, and covers 5 of 13 actions while claiming "All four"
rationale: reference.md bills itself as "Every entity, card option and action". `tapo-h500-people-card` is registered and tested but appears nowhere in reference.md or README's card table, and eight of the thirteen registered services have no reference entry. The three hardcoded counts are all wrong, which is the tell that the file was not updated as cards and services were added.
evidence: docs/reference.md:247 `Four cards ship in that one resource, so registering it makes all of them` — the table below it lists seven rows (reference.md:252-258), and www/tapo-h500-card.js:1330-1344 registers eight, including `register("tapo-h500-people-card", TapoH500PeopleCard, "Tapo H500 People",` at line 1342. docs/reference.md:337 `All six take the same options.` docs/reference.md:401 `All four actions return a response and appear under **Developer tools → Actions**.` — services.yaml declares 13 top-level services (list_recordings, download_recording, classify_downloads, delete_recording, format_hub_storage, name_face, describe_recording, daily_summary, find_face, export_recording, snooze, backup_names, restore_names) and __init__.py:730-748 registers all 13 with `supports_response=SupportsResponse.ONLY`; reference.md's `## Actions` section has only 5 `###` entries.

title: limitations.md quotes test counts that are ~10x stale and a node invocation that reports "tests 1"
rationale: The "Verification performed" section is the file whose entire purpose is being accurate about what was checked, and its two headline numbers are both wrong by an order of magnitude. The node command it prints also misreports: test_cards.mjs rolls its own `test()` helper rather than node:test, so `node --test` prints `tests 1` instead of the per-check list, which is not what the file promises.
evidence: docs/limitations.md:165 `Verified by unit test (\`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests\`, 99 tests, no` — I ran it: `Ran 1134 tests in 3.191s` / `OK`. docs/limitations.md:160 `Home Assistant (\`node --test tests/test_cards.mjs\`, 43 checks): escaping,` — `node tests/test_cards.mjs` prints 84 `ok` lines; under `node --test` the summary reads `ℹ tests 1`. tests/test_cards.mjs:46 `const test = (name, fn) => {` is the file's own harness, and its own header (tests/test_cards.mjs:4) says `node tests/test_cards.mjs`, which is also what tools/verify.sh runs.

title: limitations.md contradicts itself on how many detection codes are named, and its table still calls code 10 unknown
rationale: Within 20 lines the file says all nine codes are named and then that eight of nine are, and the table row for 10 says 'unknown' while const.py has named it 'missed doorbell' with a matching binary sensor and device trigger. A reader trying to work out whether a code needs identifying gets three different answers from one page.
evidence: docs/limitations.md:96-97 `Nine codes have been seen` / `(2, 6, 8, 9, 10, 17, 19, 20, 22) and all nine are named, each against something` versus docs/limitations.md:104 `What each code means. Eight of the nine are named, each against something` and docs/limitations.md:116 `| 10 | unknown | only ever appears beside 17, so part of the doorbell signal |`. custom_components/tapo_h500/const.py:292 `    10: "missed doorbell",`, and translations/en.json carries `binary_sensor.detected_missed_doorbell` and `device_automation.trigger_type.missed_doorbell`.

title: strings.json has drifted 102 keys behind translations/en.json and still describes a removed options form
rationale: strings.json is the conventional source-of-truth that en.json is generated from, and it is missing every `issues` and `device_automation` string, 16 entity names, and the setup step's poll_interval — while still declaring `options.step.init.data.*` fields for a step that is now `async_show_menu`. Nothing breaks today (custom integrations load translations/en.json at runtime) but verify.sh's translation check only reads en.json, so regenerating from strings.json would silently drop 102 strings. The lazy fix is either deleting strings.json or making verify.sh assert the two key sets match.
evidence: Diffing the two files: 102 flattened keys exist only in translations/en.json (all 14 `device_automation.trigger_type.*`, all `issues.*` titles/descriptions, `config.step.user.data.poll_interval`, 16 `entity.*.name` keys including `entity.button.restart.name` and `entity.update.firmware.name`), and 6 exist only in strings.json: `options.step.init.data.auto_download`, `.convert_mp4`, `.keep_downloads`, `.poll_interval` plus two data_descriptions. custom_components/tapo_h500/config_flow.py:101-103 `async def async_step_init(self, user_input=None):` / `return self.async_show_menu(` / `step_id="init",` — init is a menu, and those fields now live in `async_step_settings` (config_flow.py:301). tools/verify.sh only loads `custom_components/tapo_h500/translations/en.json` for its key check, never strings.json.

title: 18 of 31 component modules (~4,000 LOC) are never imported by any test — ast.parse is their only automated check
rationale: verify.sh's only check for these modules is a syntax parse, and their tests assert on file text rather than behaviour. A NameError, a stale `from .const import X`, or a wrong decorator argument passes the whole 1134-test gate and only fails on a real Home Assistant install at platform setup. The blocker is real (the stub harness only covers what coordinator.py imports), but it is a fixable one: `homeassistant` is stubbed as a flat module, so `homeassistant.components.*` cannot resolve.
evidence: tools/verify.sh:33-34 is the entire check for these files: `    ast.parse(path.read_text(), str(path))` / `print(f"{len(modules)} modules parse")`. tests/test_binary_sensor.py:3 states the reason: "Static, since binary_sensor.py imports the Home Assistant entity platform." and tests/test_binary_sensor.py:15 is how it substitutes: `SOURCE = (COMPONENT / "binary_sensor.py").read_text()`. I ran the existing harness (`sys.path.insert(0,"tests"); import test_coordinator`) and then tried importing each platform module; the observed results were `sensor: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'homeassistant.components'; 'homeassistant' is not a package`, identical for binary_sensor, event, switch, select, number, siren, image, camera, update; `repairs: ImportError: cannot import name 'issue_registry' from 'homeassistant.helpers'`; `entity: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'homeassistant.helpers.device_registry'`; `config_flow`/`device_trigger: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'voluptuous'`; only `diagnostics: OK`. Never-imported set (18): __init__(748), sensor(692), binary_sensor(560), repairs(376), config_flow(366), device_trigger(202), switch(159), image(143), event(141), diagnostics(124), siren(96), preview(78), number(72), update(63), select(55), camera(53), hub_control(39), entity(29) — 3,996 of 9,122 LOC. Split suggestion: `diagnostics` already imports, and the 9 platform modules need only a `homeassistant.components.<platform>` stub package; do those first.

title: verify.sh pipes the unittest run through `tail -3`, discarding the name and traceback of whatever failed
rationale: The project's own gate reports that something broke but not what, so every failure costs a second full 14-second run with the pipe removed before debugging can even start. The comment above it says the script exists so it "can gate a commit with && rather than being read by eye" — but the three lines it keeps are exactly the three that carry no diagnostic information.
evidence: tools/verify.sh:12: `python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' 2>&1 | tail -3`. I confirmed the truncation by running a deliberately failing one-test unittest through the same pipe; the complete output was `Ran 1 test in 0.000s` / (blank) / `FAILED (failures=1)` — the test name, file, line and the assertion message `'this detail is what a developer needs'` were all discarded. Fix is a few lines: capture to a variable and echo it in full when the exit status is non-zero, keeping the `tail -3` summary only on success.

title: No CI at all — the only gate is a local script a human must remember to run, on a repo HACS installs from
rationale: `tools/verify.sh` is a good gate that nothing enforces. The GitHub remote is the one HACS users install from, so a push that skips the script ships to real installs unchecked. A workflow running the existing script costs one file and adds no runtime behaviour to the integration (it never touches the hub), and the standard hassfest/HACS validation actions would have caught the strings.json drift in dx-4.
evidence: `find . -name .github -not -path './.venv/*'` returns nothing — no workflow exists. The publishable remote is real: `git remote -v` gives `github  git@github.com:Sujeom/tapo-h500-local-recordings.git (push)` alongside a LAN `origin  ssh://git@192.168.4.60:2424/...`. The gate to wire up already documents itself as commit-blocking — tools/verify.sh:2-3: `# Everything that has to pass before a commit. Exits non-zero on the first` / `# failure, so it can gate a commit with && rather than being read by eye.` Caveat for the implementer: since `origin` is the LAN server and `github` is a mirror, CI only runs on pushes that reach the mirror.

title: strings.json is dead and stale — 213 lines describing an options form that was replaced by a menu, while translations/en.json (407 lines) is the file that actually loads
rationale: Two copies of the same user-facing text, 145 keys apart, with nothing in the repo referencing or checking the older one. A developer following Home Assistant convention edits strings.json — the documented source of truth for an integration's strings — and sees no change in the UI, because the runtime reads translations/en.json. It is already wrong: it still documents the single-form options step that config_flow.py replaced with a menu.
evidence: custom_components/tapo_h500/strings.json:23-27 still has `      "init": {` / `        "title": "Tapo H500 options",` / `        "data": {` / `          "poll_interval": "Seconds between activity checks",` / `          "auto_download": "Download new recordings automatically",` — but custom_components/tapo_h500/config_flow.py:101-104 is `    async def async_step_init(self, user_input=None):` / `        return self.async_show_menu(` / ... / `            menu_options=["settings", "faces", "layout", "sensitivity"])`, and translations/en.json:53-55 correspondingly has `      "init": {` / `        "title": "Tapo H500",` / `        "menu_options": {`. Key comparison: strings.json 140 keys vs en.json 285; strings.json lacks the whole `device_automation` and `issues` sections; `options.step.init.title` differs in value between the two. `grep -rn 'strings.json' --include=*.py --include=*.sh --include=*.md --include=*.mjs .` returns zero hits, and tools/verify.sh:48-49 checks only `custom_components/tapo_h500/translations/en.json`. Either delete strings.json, or add one assertion to verify.sh that it matches en.json.

title: The shared Home Assistant stub harness lives inside test_coordinator.py and is imported for its side effect by 38 of 55 test files
rationale: A test module doubles as the fixture library for two thirds of the suite, so any change to test_coordinator.py's stub set can break dozens of unrelated files, and its name gives no hint that it is load-bearing. Extracting it to tests/harness.py is mechanical and is the natural first step before dx-1, which has to extend exactly these stubs.
evidence: tests/test_coordinator.py:36-38 defines it: `def _install_stubs():` / `    ha = types.ModuleType("homeassistant")` / `    mods = {`. Thirty-eight test files then depend on it by side effect, each with the same two lines, e.g. tests/test_snooze.py:24, tests/test_calendar.py:24 and tests/test_people.py:23: `import test_coordinator as harness  # noqa: E402  (installs the HA stubs)`; tests/test_platforms.py:26-27 spells the coupling out: `# Installs the Home Assistant stubs the component modules import.` / `import test_coordinator  # noqa: E402,F401`. Two more files do the same to test_api.py for pytapo stubs (tests/test_button.py:23, tests/test_media_health.py:33). Forty-three files also each repeat `COMPONENT = Path(__file__).parents[1] / "custom_components" / "tapo_h500"`.

title: siren_tones is fetched twice at setup by two platforms, contradicting its own docstring — the only cross-module duplicate block in the codebase
rationale: select.py and siren.py each make an independent hub round trip for the same fixed table during parallel platform setup, on hardware the project treats as fragile. api.py's docstring already asserts the property the code does not have. Caching it once (on the client instance or the coordinator) removes a startup round trip and makes the two platforms read one value.
evidence: custom_components/tapo_h500/api.py:467-471 claims: `    def siren_tones(self):` / `        """The hub's own list of siren sounds.` / ... / `        Fetched once at setup rather than every poll: it is a fixed table.` But there are two call sites — custom_components/tapo_h500/select.py:29 `        tones = await hass.async_add_executor_job(coordinator.client.siren_tones)` and custom_components/tapo_h500/siren.py:35 `        tones = await hass.async_add_executor_job(coordinator.client.siren_tones)`. A 6-line duplicate-block scan across all 31 modules found exactly two overlapping hits, both this setup body (select.py:24 / siren.py:30) — cross-module duplication is otherwise essentially absent, so this is the one real instance. Note the two callers differ deliberately on failure (select returns without adding an entity, siren falls back to `tones = []`), so a shared helper must preserve both behaviours.
